page.desc: Complete off-grid solar kits from SunGoldPower, EG4, ECO-WORTHY and Renogy, compared by prices checked today, cost per stored kWh and peak-sun hours to refill the battery.
page.answer: Short answer. The best complete off grid solar kit for a cabin or small home is the $4,949 SunGoldPower SGR-8K10E: its 3,600 W of panels refill its 10.24 kWh battery in 2.8 peak-sun hours, against 4.6 h for the 6.5 kW SGM-6510M and 9 h for Renogy's 400W kit.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Refill hours = battery Wh ÷ panel W. For the SGR-8K10E that is 10,240 ÷ 3,600 = 2.8 h. For the SGM-6510M it is 10,240 ÷ 2,220 = 4.6 h, and for the Renogy 400W kit 3,600 ÷ 400 = 9.0 h.
  • Price per stored kWh = kit price ÷ battery kWh. For the SGR-8K10E that is $4,949 ÷ 10.24 = $483. For the ECO-WORTHY 10kW it is $7,999.99 ÷ 20.48 = $391, and for the EG4 KIT-E0003 $12,476.52 ÷ 20.48 = $609.
  • SGR-8K10E vs SGR-6510E: the 8K10E costs $4,959 − $4,949 = $10 less. It has the same eight 450 W panels and the same 10.24 kWh battery, plus 8,000 − 6,500 = 1,500 W more inverter output.
  • SGR-13KM vs EG4 KIT-E0003: the same 13,000 W of output and the same 20.48 kWh. The EG4 kit costs $12,476.52 − $9,891 = $2,585.52 more. Its extra 7,560 − 6,300 = 1,260 W of older 280 W poly panels makes it only 3.3 − 2.7 = about 0.6 h faster to refill.
  • ECO-WORTHY 1560W vs Renogy 400W: the ECO-WORTHY costs $2,499.99 − $1,899.99 = $600 more. It has 1,560 ÷ 400 = 3.9× the panels and 5.12 ÷ 3.6 = 1.4× the storage, and refills in 3.3 h instead of 9.0 h.

Peak-sun hours to refill: the figure kit listings leave out

A kit's panels have to refill its battery between one night and the next. Battery watt-hours divided by panel watts gives the hours of full sun (peak-sun hours) the kit needs to go from empty to full. That figure assumes no losses and no daytime load. Real charging takes longer, because heat, wiring and charging losses cut panel output, and anything running during the day uses part of the harvest. A kit whose refill time is longer than the sun hours you actually get in winter can't recover from one cloudy day.

The makers' own sun-hour bases show the gap. SunGoldPower rates the SGR-8K10E at about 14.4 kWh a day from 4 hours of full sun (3,600 W × 4 h), which is more than its 10.24 kWh battery. On the same 4-hour basis the SGM-6510M makes 2,220 W × 4 h = 8.9 kWh, which is less than its own 10.24 kWh battery. Renogy bases its kits on 5–6 peak-sun hours, and at that rate the 400W kit makes 2.0–2.4 kWh a day against a 3.6 kWh battery, so a full refill takes 1.5–1.8 days.

Room to add panels matters as well. The SGR-8K10E's inverter accepts up to 11,000 W of PV on two MPPT inputs, about three times the 3,600 W it ships with, so the refill time can be cut later. The 3,500 W all-in-one inverter in the ECO-WORTHY 1560W kit lists 4,400 W maximum PV input and 145 VDC maximum open-circuit voltage on its own product page, so that kit has much less room to grow. To buy the pick: {buy:sungoldpower-sgr-8k10e-off-grid-solar-kit}.

Not recommended

SunGoldPower SGM-6510M ($4,703). It has the same 6.5 kW inverter and 10.24 kWh battery as the SGR-6510E, but only 2,220 W of panels, so it needs 4.6 peak-sun hours to refill. That is more than one day at SunGoldPower's own 4-hour basis. For $4,949 − $4,703 = $246 more, the SGR-8K10E refills in 2.8 h and adds 1,500 W of inverter output.
